provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Back to art
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name art tools.
The pupils should be able to explain how to care for art tools.
Introduction:
Last term we did art with our hands.
Today we learn about our tools.
Content:
Art tools are crayons, pencils, scissors and glue.
We care for tools by keeping them dry.
We put them in a box after use.
Class activity:
Let's pass crayons around and say their names.
Then we put them back in the box carefully.
Evaluation questions:
Name one art tool.
How do we take care of scissors?
What do we use to draw?
Summary:
Art tools help us make beautiful things.
We must take good care of them.

topics.title: Drawing with shapes
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify square, triangle and rectangle.
The pupils should be able to draw a house using shapes.
Introduction:
We know shapes like circle and square.
Today we use shapes to draw.
Content:
A house has a square body and triangle roof.
A bus has rectangle body and circle wheels.
We draw by putting shapes together.
Class activity:
Let's trace squares and triangles with our fingers.
Then we draw a house on paper with shapes.
Evaluation questions:
What shape has three sides?
Which shape is good for a bus body?
Draw a house with a triangle roof.
Summary:
Shapes can make pictures of things we see every day.

topics.title: Patterns
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify stripes, dots and zigzag patterns.
The pupils should be able to decorate a shirt with patterns.
Introduction:
We see patterns on our clothes.
Today we make our own patterns.
Content:
Stripes are lines going up and down.
Dots are small circles in a row.
Zigzag is like lightning going side to side.
Class activity:
Let's clap stripes, tap dots and zigzag with our hands.
Then we decorate a paper shirt with patterns.
Evaluation questions:
Show me a zigzag pattern with your fingers.
What pattern is on your school uniform?
How many dots can you draw?
Summary:
Patterns make clothes look nice and colorful.

topics.title: Primary colours
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to name the primary colours.
The pupils should be able to sort objects by colour.
Introduction:
Colours make our world beautiful.
Today we learn about primary colours.
Content:
The primary colours are red, yellow and blue.
Red is like ripe tomatoes.
Yellow is like ripe mangoes.
Blue is like the sky.
Class activity:
Let's point to red objects in the classroom.
Then we sort toys into red, yellow and blue groups.
Evaluation questions:
Name the three primary colours.
What colour is a ripe plantain?
Which colour is like the sky?
Summary:
Red, yellow and blue are the main colours.

topics.title: Secondary colours
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to mix primary colours to make secondary colours.
The pupils should be able to paint a colour wheel flower.
Introduction:
We know red, yellow and blue.
Today we mix them to make new colours.
Content:
Red and yellow make orange like a ripe pawpaw.
Yellow and blue make green like plant leaves.
Blue and red make purple like some flowers.
Class activity:
Let's mix paint to see orange, green and purple.
Then we paint a flower with these colours.
Evaluation questions:
What colour do red and yellow make?
Which colour is made from blue and yellow?
Show me how to make purple.
Summary:
Mixing primary colours makes beautiful new colours.

topics.title: Clay animals
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to mould clay into animal shapes.
The pupils should be able to add details to clay animals.
Introduction:
We have seen many animals in pictures.
Today we make animals with clay.
Content:
Clay is soft and we can shape it.
First we roll clay to make the body.
Then we add ears, tail and face.
Class activity:
Let's roll clay in our hands to make it soft.
Then we make our favourite animal and add details.
Evaluation questions:
What can we make with clay?
What part do we add to a cat?
How do we make clay soft?
Summary:
Clay is fun for making animal shapes.

topics.title: Paper plate masks
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make an animal mask from a paper plate.
The pupils should be able to cut eyes and add features to a mask.
Introduction:
We wear masks during festivals.
Today we make animal masks.
Content:
We use a paper plate as the face.
We cut holes for eyes to see.
We add whiskers, nose and ears.
Class activity:
Let's draw animal faces on paper plates.
Then we cut eyes and add features with paper.
Evaluation questions:
What do we use for the mask face?
Where do we cut holes on the mask?
What animal mask would you like to make?
Summary:
We can make fun masks from paper plates.

topics.title: Tie and dye play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make patterns with rubber bands.
The pupils should be able to dye cloth and see the patterns.
Introduction:
We see tie and dye clothes at the market.
Today we try tie and dye play.
Content:
We fold cloth and put rubber bands on it.
The bands make patterns when we dye.
When we open it, we see the surprise pattern.
Class activity:
Let's fold cloth and put rubber bands on it.
Then we dip in dye and open to see our patterns.
Evaluation questions:
What do we use to make patterns?
What happens when we open the dyed cloth?
Which pattern do you like best?
Summary:
Tie and dye makes beautiful patterns on cloth.

topics.title: Collage of Nigeria
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify the Nigerian flag colours.
The pupils should be able to make a flag collage.
Introduction:
The Nigerian flag has green and white.
Today we make a flag collage.
Content:
The Nigerian flag has two green sides.
The middle is white.
We use paper to make our flag.
Class activity:
Let's look at the Nigerian flag.
Then we make a flag with green and white paper.
Evaluation questions:
What colour is on the Nigerian flag?
What does the green stand for?
How many colours are in the flag?
Summary:
We can make our flag with paper collage.

topics.title: Art exhibition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to mount their art works.
The pupils should be able to talk about their favourite art.
Introduction:
We have made many art works this term.
Today we show them to our friends.
Content:
We put our best works on display.
We walk around to see others' works.
We can say what we like about each work.
Class activity:
Let's choose three best works to display.
Then we walk around and look at everyone's art.
Evaluation questions:
Which work is your best?
What do you like about your friend's work?
How do we show respect for art?
Summary:
We are proud of our art works.
